bugs.summary: stock check and reservation are read-then-write in Python (available() on the loaded product, then product.reserved = product.reserved + qty), with no lock or conditional UPDATE, so concurrent orders oversell
bugs.repro: product has on_hand=1; two customers POST /orders for 1 unit at the same time; both load the product with reserved=0 before either commits, both pass the check and write reserved=1; two orders are placed for one unit (reserved=1, two held reservations)

bugs.summary: on a declined card the order goes to payment_failed but the stock reserved just before is never released; payment_failed is in FINAL_STATES so cancel refuses it and the sweeper only looks at placed orders, so the units stay reserved forever
bugs.repro: product on_hand=1; POST /orders with card_token tok_decline -> payment_failed; GET /products/1 shows reserved=1, available=0; POST /orders/{id}/cancel -> 409; expire_unconfirmed_orders does not touch it; nobody can buy the unit again

bugs.summary: cancel is allowed from OPEN_STATES, which includes shipped, so a customer can cancel an order that has already left the warehouse and gets a full refund
bugs.repro: place, confirm, ship an order; customer POST /orders/{id}/cancel -> 200 cancelled and the captured payment is refunded in full while the parcel is with the carrier

bugs.summary: approve only refuses rejected returns, not already-approved ones, so approving twice refunds and restocks twice
bugs.repro: delivered order of 3 x 1000; return 1 unit; staff POST /returns/{id}/approve twice (double click) -> two refunds of 1000 at the gateway and on_hand goes up by 2

bugs.summary: a packing event sets status=packing unconditionally (only cancelled/payment_failed are refused), so a late or redelivered packing webhook moves a shipped or delivered order back to packing
bugs.repro: confirm order; warehouse sends shipped, then a delayed packing event arrives; GET /orders/{id} shows status packing instead of shipped (and the order can now be shipped or cancelled again)

bugs.summary: creating a return loads the order by id without checking it belongs to the calling customer (customer_id is taken but never compared), unlike the order routes
bugs.repro: alice's order 1 is delivered; mallory POST /orders/1/returns with X-Customer-Id: mallory -> 201, a return (and later refund) is filed against alice's order

bugs.summary: ship is allowed from placed, skipping confirm, so goods leave the warehouse with the payment only authorized, never captured
bugs.repro: place an order (payment authorized); staff POST /orders/{id}/ship -> 200 shipped with captured_cents=0; the authorization can expire and the shop is never paid

bugs.summary: the remaining-to-return check reads returned_quantity() then inserts the new return with no lock or constraint, so two concurrent return requests for the same line both pass
bugs.repro: delivered order with 1 unit; the customer submits the return form twice at once; both requests read returned=0, both insert, two returns for one unit exist and both can be approved

decoys.why_correct: _transition is a compare-and-swap: UPDATE ... WHERE status IN (allowed) and it checks rowcount, so concurrent confirm/cancel/ship calls cannot both win; confirm_order treats a lost race to confirmed as an idempotent success without capturing again

the idempotency lookup is check-then-insert, but (customer_id, idempotency_key) is a unique constraint and the IntegrityError path rolls back and returns the winner's order, so concurrent retries create one order

release flips the reservation held->released with a conditional UPDATE, checks rowcount, and only then decrements reserved with a SQL-side expression, so a double cancel or cancel+sweeper releases stock once
